title: City of Greed
text: “Well then, I’m sure you’ve heard the rumors, but it’d be a big help if you’d buy some of our goods.”
“It’s a food sale pulled by the Divine Bird’s carriage! Everyone! Rejoice!”

Once the commotion caused by Father’s imposter dies down, the villagers will swarm the food. After all, they’re in a pretty dire financial situation. I seem to recall hearing that even in the first world—the one before I started looping—food shortages were a constant problem around this time. They say it was all the fault of the waves.

Well, Father’s land development and efforts toward food self-sufficiency completely solved the problem afterward. For now, though, gaining their trust is the top priority. Father went back into the back of the wagon. But at the same time, he beckoned his Assistant over.
“Okay?　Wyndia, you really shouldn’t go around imitating me to scare people.”
“But… I was tricking the Shield Hero… and I just couldn’t help myself…”
“I appreciate the sentiment, mind you. But if you start doing things like that as a matter of course, I won’t be able to face your father.”

At first, the assistant looked displeased by Father’s words, but when he said he wouldn’t be able to face her father, she let her animal ears droop, looking dejected. From what I’ve heard, he seemed to dote on her. Father told me later that the Assistant must have thought she wanted to grow up just as her late father had wished.
“…I’m sorry.”
“It’s fine as long as you truly reflect on it. Just be careful next time.”
“Yes…”
“Gau!”
“Gaelion-chan, too!”
“Gau?”
The monster, however, seemed completely unfazed. I won’t forget it, though. I remember what he said while Kou was getting scolded.
“Seriously…”
The assistant is gently petting the monster’s head. The monster has grown quite a bit, hasn’t it? According to Father, it’s sharp and clever.

I find it hard to believe a dragon could be that smart. I’ve subtly pointed out to Sakura-chan that she has a ten-yen-coin-sized bald spot. It’s probably because having the dragon nearby is causing her stress. Father is currently trying to figure out a way to help her relieve that stress without making a big deal out of it.

After that, Keel and the Lazy Pig are working as vendors as usual, peddling ingredients. However… it seems there’s been an uptick in activity from impostors posing as the Shield Hero. We’re hearing about such incidents more and more wherever we go.
“Where shall we go next?”
“Maybe up north… According to Elena, we can get a good price there.”

Well, either way, we just need to hang in there a little longer. So, when we headed to a town up north, we came across one that didn’t accept commercial waybills. The Father had a brief conversation with the gatekeeper. Reluctantly, he seems to have given up on entering the town and decided to take a detour. The carriage jolted along as we headed toward the next town—one that looked a bit run-down.
“Something’s… off about the townspeople, isn’t it?”
“Yeah, something’s weird.”
My father and Keel were looking out the carriage window.
“Is that so?”
Honestly, I couldn’t make head or tail of the change at all.
“Yeah, it’s like everyone’s distracted, or maybe they just look dissatisfied…”
Just then, a man and a pig—who were drawing quite a bit of attention—walked by carrying a money bag. Father watched the scene in silence.
“I wonder what that’s about? I hear there’s a terribly greedy noble in that direction.”
“Maybe they’re out shopping?”
“I wonder? Oh well, never mind. Keel, get ready to open up the shop.”
“Got it, big bro. Hey, Elena, stop sleeping and get ready to open the shop!”
“Boo…”

Keel and the Lazy Pig have started getting the shop ready. Lately, the accessories I’ve made—merchandise modeled after Filolial-sama—have been selling well. But… this village is pretty stingy, isn’t it? They come to look, but they never actually buy anything. Even my father is starting to get suspicious and is keeping an eye on the situation.
“Bro, I figured out why nobody’s coming. Apparently, the people in this village don’t have any money at all.”
After Keel agreed to a barter and sold some food and medicine, he told my father:
“What happened?”
“Apparently, this town gets raided by bandits a lot, and there’s a lot of looting. So they asked the folks from the neighboring town to send bodyguards—”

To summarize Keel’s story, it seems the people from the neighboring town often interfere with trade and business. The townspeople have reluctantly had to make frequent trips to the neighboring town to stock up on supplies, which has inevitably drained their funds. To make matters worse, for some reason, bandit raids have become increasingly frequent, and they’re really struggling. They tried to hire bodyguards to protect them from the bandit raids, but it turns out those bodyguards were actually the bandits themselves. Apparently, there are all sorts of complicated circumstances involved.
“So?”
“Those guys from earlier seem to be nobles from this town.”
“I hate to say it, but they looked like they were down on their luck… So what?”
“Apparently, their daughter was used as collateral for a loan from a noble in the neighboring town, and everyone chipped in to pay it off.”
“If the townspeople are pooling their money like that, they must be good people. So that’s why… everyone’s just looking but can’t afford to buy anything.”
“Seems so. They say they’re not struggling to put food on the table yet, but they’re out of money.”
“Hmm… I wish I could do something to help, but if I make a move, I’ll be exposed as the Shield Hero, and then I won’t be able to do anything at all. I wonder what to do.”
My father muttered, looking troubled. It’s quite a difficult problem, isn’t it?
“Well, the sun’s starting to set, so let’s stay in this town for the night.”
“Got it!”
That evening, while everyone was resting at the inn, the townspeople were making a commotion in the town square.
“I wonder what’s going on?”
Father discreetly headed toward the square to find out what was happening.
“Did something happen?”
“Ah… well…”
We approached as well and listened in.
“We were told the noble would be back by nightfall… but we haven’t heard a peep… so we were just discussing whether to go investigate…”
“Hmm… The next town is a bit far, isn’t it? Plus, the sun’s already set… Considering not only monsters but also the possibility of a nighttime bandit raid, wouldn’t that be difficult?”

Marching at night is quite dangerous, after all. The rate of monster appearances skyrockets, so unless you’re confident in your skills, it could be a matter of life and death. Well, in my first world, I used to level up at night. Either way, if someone with no combat experience goes out there, they’ll be lucky to get away with just a few injuries.
“We do have a few people skilled in martial arts, but their wounds from fighting bandits haven’t fully healed yet…”
“Hmm…”
My father rests his hand on his chin, deep in thought.
“…We’ll go check it out.”
“The Holy Ones of the Divine Bird? Is that all right?”
“Ah, I had some business to take care of anyway, so this works out perfectly. We’ll provide an escort.”
“Could we ask you to do that?”
“Leave it to us. Just make sure you don’t do anything dangerous. I’m sure the nobles you trust feel the same way.”
“Y-yes! It’s a huge relief to know the Holy Ones will be escorting us.”
And so, my father volunteered to provide an escort for the townspeople.
“Did everyone hear that?”
My father turned around and asked, and everyone nodded. Oh, the Lazy Pig is already fast asleep at the inn.
“So, let’s go.”
“Got it, big bro!”
“Sakura and the others will do their best, too.”
It was decided that Sakura and the others would pull the town’s carriage.
“It seems there’s a chance bandits might come to plunder, so Motoyasu, Yuki, Kou, Wyndia, and Gaelion, you guys stay behind.”
“Got it!”
My father-in-law and the others loaded the townspeople onto the wagons and set off for the neighboring town. A few hours later… well into the night, they returned.
“We’re back.”
“How did it go?”

“Hmm… I was worried they might have run into some danger, but they were just hanging out normally in the neighboring town. And… I happened to spot Itsuki there, too. Apparently, they were making plans to take down that noble over there tonight.”
“I see…”
“I tried to keep my distance so as not to get too involved… but I was in a bit of a bind when some townspeople almost started talking to me.”
“Was everything okay?”
“Yeah, by tomorrow… I’m sure it’ll all be settled.”

According to my Father, they were splitting up to search for the town’s noble when they spotted Itsuki and his group at a tavern. They approached casually to listen in on their conversation and nearly tripped over themselves.
“Itsuki… seems to be acting like some kind of ‘General of Social Reform.’”
“Come to think of it, I never heard anything about Itsuki making a big splash in the future.”
“Huh? Really? It’s causing quite a stir, actually. They say he’s hiding his identity while dispensing justice.”

That’s strange. I heard that in the future, the whole country was abuzz with excitement over Ren and my exploits. Aside from that, the only other topic my Father mentioned was that the Holy One of the Divine Bird was performing miracles all over the place, wasn’t it?
